newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak central bank, Nomura sign agreement.
newsitem.headline: Slovak central bank, Nomura sign agreement.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Tuesday said it had signed a financial advisory services agreement with Nomura International Plc, though it had no immediate need to issue its bonds abroad.
"NBS Governor Vladimir Masar and Nomura's top representative Hitosi Tonomura have signed a cooperation agreement, under which Nomura becomes the NBS's financial adviser," the NBS said in a statement.
Nomura has advised the NBS since 1993, and has lead-managed two bond issues to support Slovakia's balance of payments.

"So far, the country's widening current account deficit has not affected foreign exchange reserves, and I see no reason for any bond issue speculation," Peter Balaz, head of the NBS Foreing Exchange Liabilities Department, told Reuters.

"But on the other hand, the cooperation with Nomura has been good, and thus it was formalised," Balaz said. "It is (still) a loose relationship though, and no advantages or disadvantages for Nomura emerge from this agreement."
The Slovak current account deficit for the first seven months of 1996 was $847.2 million, while the capital account had a surplus of $949.9 million.
